references.sentence: In “linear” phase detectors such as that in [6], the output pulsewidth is linearly proportional to the input phase difference, resulting in a constant loop gain during lock Fig. 8.

By contrast, bang-bang PDs [5] employ simple flipflops for maximum speed but provide only two output states [Fig. 8(a)], creating significant ripple on the control line in the locked condition and hence producing great jitter at the VCO output.
Shown in Fig. 8(b), the PD is realized as a master–slave sample-and-hold circuit (an “analog D-flipflop”), whereby each rising data transition samples the instantaneous value of the VCO output.
